title_short: Angela Harrell · Where Are My Jordans?
headline: Kids at a 4EveryKid giveaway ask for Jordans by name, because a brand-name pair is how a kid facing homelessness gets to blend in.
story: Angela laughs about the tough customers: kids asking where their Jordans are, or if there are any Nikes. In the end everyone leaves happy. Some wear them out the door, some keep the box to share the thrill with their family.

4EveryKid puts new branded athletic shoes on kids experiencing homelessness. In the United States that is 1.5 million kids. All kids just want to be like everyone else: try out for the team, run track, get to school safely.

Loops: L1 “Who is asking for Jordans?” opens at 0:00 and closes on “Some kids want to wear their shoes right out.” L2 “Why does a brand-name shoe matter so much?” opens at 0:00 and closes in the button: they get to hold their head up a little higher and blend in, “because that's all you really want to do as a kid anyway.”

[01:42.7] of their journey.

[02:06.6] families economically through our collection of used shoes and clothing, individuals are

[03:31.6] So doing this work makes me feel such a sense of gratitude.

[03:41.4] [left out: a line about Voya as a company]
[03:49.5] Community is really important.
